An apparatus is provided for delivering a bolus of a medical agent to a patient. The apparatus comprises a pump mechanism, a data input device, and a processor in data communication with the keypad and configured to control the pump mechanism. The processor is programmed to receive, through the data port, data specifying a bolus amount; receive, through the data port, data relating to a duration; receive, through the data port, a percentage defining a portion of the bolus amount to be delivered immediately upon execution of a delivery command and a remainder of the bolus amount to be delivered over the duration upon execution of the delivery command; and execute the delivery command, thereby controlling the pump mechanism to deliver the bolus.

Also provided is a method of temporarily adjusting the delivery rate of an infusion pump, wherein the infusion pump is programmed to deliver a basal rate. The method comprises prompting a user to select whether to enter the temporary rate as a percentage of the current delivery rate or as a new delivery rate; entering into the pump a period of time having a beginning and an end; entering into the pump a temporary basal rate; and delivering the therapeutic agent at a delivery rate substantially equal to the temporary basal rate during the period of time.

A device is provided for administering a bolus dose of a medical substance to a patient. The device includes a pumping mechanism, a data entry component, and a processor that communicates with the keypad and is configured to operate the pumping mechanism. The processor is configured to accept, through the data port, information identifying the bolus quantity; accept, through the data port, information identifying a delivery duration; and accept, through the data port, a percentage value. This percentage indicates how much of the bolus quantity is to be delivered at once when a delivery command is carried out, with the remaining portion of the bolus quantity being administered over the specified duration after the delivery command is executed. The processor then performs the delivery command and controls the pumping mechanism to dispense the bolus.

A method is also provided for temporarily changing the delivery rate of an infusion pump. The infusion pump is set to administer a basal rate. The method includes asking the user to choose whether the temporary rate will be entered as a percentage of the existing delivery rate or as a replacement delivery rate; inputting into the pump a time interval with a defined start and finish; inputting a temporary basal rate into the pump; and administering the therapeutic agent at a rate approximately equal to the temporary basal rate throughout that time interval.

The apparatus is configured to deliver a bolus of a medical agent to a patient by means of a pump mechanism controlled by a processor. The pump mechanism may be operated in accordance with instructions generated by the processor so that a programmed quantity of the medical agent is delivered to the patient in a controlled and reliable manner.

In operation, the processor receives programming information relating to the bolus delivery. This information may include a bolus amount, a delivery duration, and percentage data. The information can be entered through a data input device, such as a user interface, keypad, touchscreen, or other control element, or it may be received through a data port from an external device or system.

The percentage data determines how the total bolus amount is divided between an immediate delivery portion and an extended delivery portion. For example, the percentage may specify the portion of the bolus that is to be delivered promptly or substantially immediately, while the remaining portion is delivered gradually over the specified duration. In this way, the apparatus can provide a combined bolus delivery profile that includes both an immediate component and a time-extended component.

After receiving the bolus amount, duration, and percentage data, the processor executes a delivery command. The delivery command controls operation of the pump mechanism so that the programmed bolus is delivered according to the selected parameters. The processor may regulate the timing and rate of pump actuation to ensure that the immediate portion and the extended portion of the bolus are administered as programmed.

The method also allows a user to temporarily adjust an infusion pump’s basal delivery rate for a specified period of time. This temporary basal adjustment enables the user to increase, decrease, or otherwise modify the normal basal infusion rate without permanently changing the underlying basal delivery schedule. Once the specified period has elapsed, the pump may return to the previously programmed basal rate.
outputs.L4:
A medical infusion pump apparatus and associated method are provided for delivering a therapeutic agent, such as insulin or another medication, in a controlled and programmable manner. The apparatus includes a reservoir or other source of the therapeutic agent, a pumping mechanism for moving the agent from the reservoir to a patient through an infusion set or delivery path, a processor or controller for governing pump operation, and a data input device through which a user may enter delivery instructions. The data input device may include buttons, a keypad, a touchscreen, a remote controller, a connected computing device, or another suitable user interface. A display or other output device may also be provided to present programming options, confirmation prompts, delivery status, alarms, and historical delivery information.

The processor is configured to receive user-entered information relating to bolus delivery. In one mode, the user may program an immediate bolus in which a selected amount of the therapeutic agent is delivered promptly after confirmation. In another mode, the user may program an extended bolus in which all or part of the selected bolus amount is delivered over a user-defined period of time. The pump may also support a combination bolus or dual-wave bolus, in which a first portion of the bolus is delivered substantially immediately and a second portion is delivered gradually over a specified duration. For example, a patient may enter a total bolus amount, designate a percentage or amount to be delivered immediately, and designate the remaining amount to be delivered over a selected time interval. The processor then controls the pumping mechanism to deliver the immediate portion and to distribute the extended portion according to the programmed schedule.

The apparatus may further allow programming of temporary basal rate adjustments. A basal rate is a continuing or background delivery rate of the therapeutic agent, and the temporary basal function permits that rate to be modified for a limited period without permanently changing the patient’s stored basal profile. The user may enter the temporary basal adjustment in different ways. In one option, the adjustment may be entered as a percentage of the current basal rate, such as increasing the rate to 150% or decreasing it to 50% for a selected duration. In another option, the user may enter a new temporary basal rate directly, such as a specified number of units per hour or other delivery-rate value. The processor calculates and applies the appropriate delivery rate for the selected time period and then automatically returns the pump to the previously programmed basal rate or basal profile when the temporary interval expires.

The method of operating the pump includes receiving delivery parameters through the data input device, validating or confirming the parameters, calculating the delivery schedule, and controlling the pumping mechanism according to that schedule. The method may include receiving a total bolus amount, receiving an immediate portion and an extended portion, receiving an extended delivery duration, and delivering the therapeutic agent accordingly. The method may also include receiving a temporary basal command, determining whether the command is expressed as a percentage of the current basal rate or as an absolute new rate, applying the temporary rate for the user-selected duration, and restoring the prior basal delivery program after completion.

Safety and usability features may be incorporated into the apparatus and method. The processor may compare entered values against programmed limits, maximum bolus amounts, maximum basal rates, minimum delivery rates, or patient-specific therapy settings. The pump may request confirmation before beginning delivery and may provide alerts if a programmed value exceeds a threshold, if delivery is interrupted, if the reservoir is low, or if an occlusion or other fault is detected. Delivery data may be stored in memory for later review by the patient, caregiver, or clinician.

By allowing bolus delivery to be divided into immediate and extended portions and by permitting temporary basal rates to be entered either as a percentage of the current rate or as an absolute replacement rate, the infusion pump provides a flexible platform for individualized therapy. This flexibility can be useful in situations where medication needs vary over time, such as meals with different absorption profiles, exercise, illness, stress, or other patient-specific conditions. The result is a more customizable and programmable infusion system that can better match therapeutic agent delivery to the needs of the patient over defined durations.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an apparatus and method for a medical infusion pump, including processor-controlled bolus delivery with a split immediate portion and remainder delivered over time, plus a temporary basal rate feature.
counterfactuals.output:
An apparatus for delivering a medical fluid, such as insulin or another therapeutic agent, may include a reservoir, a pumping mechanism, an infusion set or delivery conduit, user-interface controls, one or more sensors, and a processor-based controller configured to execute stored delivery instructions.

The pump may be configured to provide both programmable bolus delivery and programmable basal delivery, including a temporary basal-rate adjustment.

## Apparatus

The infusion pump may include:

1. **Fluid reservoir**
   - A cartridge, syringe, bag, or other container holding the therapeutic fluid.

2. **Drive mechanism**
   - A motor, piston, peristaltic mechanism, lead screw, piezoelectric pump, or other actuator capable of delivering controlled increments of fluid from the reservoir.

3. **Delivery path**
   - Tubing, cannula, catheter, or infusion set connecting the reservoir to the patient.

4. **Processor and memory**
   - A microcontroller or processor coupled to non-transitory memory storing:
     - basal-rate schedules,
     - bolus-delivery algorithms,
     - temporary basal-rate parameters,
     - safety limits,
     - delivery history,
     - alarm logic.

5. **User interface**
   - Buttons, touchscreen, display, wireless interface, or remote controller permitting a user or clinician to enter delivery parameters.

6. **Power source**
   - A battery or rechargeable power supply.

7. **Sensors and safety components**
   - Optional occlusion detection, motor-position sensing, reservoir-volume sensing, battery monitoring, dose-limit checking, and alarm or notification devices.

## Processor-Controlled Split Bolus Delivery

The processor may be configured to receive a bolus request representing a total bolus amount. The bolus may be divided into:

1. **An immediate portion**
   - Delivered promptly after confirmation.

2. **A remainder portion**
   - Delivered gradually over a selected time period.

For example, the user may enter:

- total bolus amount,
- percentage or amount to deliver immediately,
- duration over which the remaining amount is to be delivered,
- optional delivery profile, such as constant, stepped, or variable rate.

The processor calculates:

- immediate bolus amount = total bolus × selected immediate fraction,
- extended bolus amount = total bolus − immediate bolus amount,
- extended delivery rate = extended bolus amount / selected duration, unless another profile is selected.

The processor then commands the drive mechanism to deliver the immediate portion and schedules the remainder for delivery over the specified time interval.

The remainder may be delivered as a series of small pulses, micro-boluses, or continuous pump increments at intervals determined by the controller.

## Temporary Basal Rate Feature

The pump may also include a temporary basal function. A basal rate is a background delivery rate maintained over time according to a stored schedule. The temporary basal feature permits the scheduled basal rate to be temporarily modified.

The processor may receive a temporary basal command including one or more of:

- temporary basal duration,
- temporary basal rate,
- percentage increase or decrease relative to the programmed basal rate,
- start time,
- cancellation instruction.

During the temporary basal interval, the processor overrides or modifies the normal basal schedule and commands delivery according to the temporary setting. After expiration of the temporary basal interval, the processor automatically returns to the programmed basal schedule.

For example:

- Normal basal rate: 1.0 unit/hour
- Temporary basal setting: 50% for 2 hours
- Delivered basal rate during interval: 0.5 unit/hour
- After 2 hours: pump resumes normal basal schedule

Alternatively:

- Normal basal rate: 1.0 unit/hour
- Temporary basal setting: 150% for 3 hours
- Delivered basal rate: 1.5 units/hour
- After 3 hours: normal basal delivery resumes

## Method of Operation

A method of operating the infusion pump may include:

1. **Receiving basal schedule data**
   - The processor stores one or more scheduled basal rates in memory.

2. **Receiving a bolus command**
   - The pump receives a total bolus amount and split-bolus parameters.

3. **Determining bolus portions**
   - The processor calculates an immediate portion and a delayed or extended portion.

4. **Delivering the immediate bolus**
   - The processor actuates the drive mechanism to deliver the immediate portion.

5. **Scheduling the remainder**
   - The processor determines delivery increments and timing for the remainder.

6. **Delivering the remainder over time**
   - The controller periodically actuates the pump mechanism to deliver the extended portion over the selected duration.

7. **Providing basal delivery**
   - The processor independently maintains basal delivery according to the active basal schedule, subject to temporary basal modifications.

8. **Receiving a temporary basal command**
   - The pump receives a temporary basal rate or percentage and a duration.

9. **Applying the temporary basal rate**
   - During the temporary interval, the processor adjusts basal delivery according to the temporary basal command.

10. **Returning to scheduled basal delivery**
   - Upon expiration or cancellation of the temporary basal interval, the processor resumes the programmed basal schedule.

## Coordination of Bolus and Basal Delivery

The processor may coordinate basal and bolus delivery so that both are accurately tracked. The extended bolus delivery may occur concurrently with basal delivery. In that case, the controller may calculate a combined delivery command for each time interval, including:

- scheduled or temporary basal amount, plus
- any extended bolus amount due during that interval.

The pump may record each delivered increment in memory and may display remaining bolus amount, remaining bolus duration, active temporary basal status, and total fluid delivered.

## Safety Features

The apparatus may include safety logic configured to:

- prevent delivery exceeding programmed maximum bolus limits,
- prevent basal rates outside allowed limits,
- confirm user-entered values before delivery,
- detect occlusions or motor errors,
- suspend delivery upon fault detection,
- alarm on low reservoir, low battery, or delivery interruption,
- allow cancellation of an active extended bolus or temporary basal setting,
- log delivery events for review.

In this way, the infusion pump provides processor-controlled delivery of a bolus having an immediate component and an extended component while also supporting temporary modification of basal delivery for a defined period.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft claims-like language for an insulin pump invention where the user enters bolus amount, duration, and percentage to control delivery, and can temporarily adjust basal delivery as either a percent or new rate.
counterfactuals.output:
Below is sample **claims-like language** for an insulin pump invention. This is drafting-style text only and not legal advice.

---

## Example Claim Set

### 1. Insulin Delivery System

1. An insulin delivery system comprising:  
   a pump mechanism configured to deliver insulin from a reservoir to a user;  
   a user interface configured to receive user input;  
   one or more processors; and  
   memory storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the insulin delivery system to:  
   receive, via the user interface, a bolus amount;  
   receive, via the user interface, a bolus duration;  
   receive, via the user interface, a bolus percentage;  
   determine a first portion of the bolus amount based on the bolus percentage and a second portion of the bolus amount based on a remainder of the bolus percentage;  
   control the pump mechanism to deliver the first portion of the bolus amount according to a first delivery profile; and  
   control the pump mechanism to deliver the second portion of the bolus amount over the bolus duration according to a second delivery profile.

### 2. Dependent Claims

2. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the first delivery profile comprises substantially immediate delivery of the first portion.

3. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the second delivery profile comprises delivery of the second portion at a substantially constant rate over the bolus duration.

4. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the bolus percentage represents a percentage of the bolus amount to be delivered substantially immediately.

5. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the bolus percentage represents a percentage of the bolus amount to be delivered over the bolus duration.

6. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the insulin delivery system to display, before delivery, at least one of the first portion, the second portion, the bolus duration, or a calculated delivery rate.

7. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the insulin delivery system to receive a confirmation input before initiating delivery of the bolus amount.

---

### 3. Temporary Basal Adjustment

8. The insulin delivery system of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the insulin delivery system to:  
   receive a temporary basal adjustment input;  
   receive a temporary basal duration;  
   determine whether the temporary basal adjustment input represents a percentage adjustment relative to a programmed basal rate or a new basal delivery rate; and  
   control the pump mechanism to deliver basal insulin during the temporary basal duration according to the temporary basal adjustment input.

9. The insulin delivery system of claim 8, wherein, when the temporary basal adjustment input represents the percentage adjustment, the instructions cause the insulin delivery system to calculate a temporary basal rate by multiplying the programmed basal rate by a factor corresponding to the percentage adjustment.

10. The insulin delivery system of claim 8, wherein, when the temporary basal adjustment input represents the new basal delivery rate, the instructions cause the insulin delivery system to deliver basal insulin at the new basal delivery rate during the temporary basal duration.

11. The insulin delivery system of claim 8, wherein the instructions further cause the insulin delivery system to resume the programmed basal rate after expiration of the temporary basal duration.

12. The insulin delivery system of claim 8, wherein the user interface is configured to permit user selection between a percentage-based temporary basal mode and a rate-based temporary basal mode.

13. The insulin delivery system of claim 8, wherein the temporary basal duration is user-entered.

14. The insulin delivery system of claim 8, wherein the instructions further cause the insulin delivery system to display an indication of whether the temporary basal adjustment is being applied as a percentage adjustment or as a new basal delivery rate.

---

## Method Claims

### 15. Method of Delivering Insulin

15. A method of operating an insulin pump, the method comprising:  
   receiving, by the insulin pump, a user-entered bolus amount;  
   receiving, by the insulin pump, a user-entered bolus duration;  
   receiving, by the insulin pump, a user-entered bolus percentage;  
   determining, by the insulin pump, a first bolus portion and a second bolus portion based on the bolus amount and the bolus percentage;  
   delivering, by the insulin pump, the first bolus portion according to a first delivery schedule; and  
   delivering, by the insulin pump, the second bolus portion over the bolus duration according to a second delivery schedule.

16. The method of claim 15, wherein delivering the first bolus portion comprises delivering the first bolus portion substantially immediately.

17. The method of claim 15, wherein delivering the second bolus portion comprises delivering the second bolus portion substantially evenly over the bolus duration.

18. The method of claim 15, further comprising displaying a bolus summary comprising at least one of the bolus amount, the bolus percentage, the bolus duration, the first bolus portion, or the second bolus portion.

---

### 19. Method of Temporary Basal Delivery

19. The method of claim 15, further comprising:  
   receiving, by the insulin pump, a temporary basal command;  
   receiving, by the insulin pump, a temporary basal duration;  
   receiving, by the insulin pump, a temporary basal value;  
   determining whether the temporary basal value corresponds to a percentage of a programmed basal rate or to a new basal rate;  
   delivering basal insulin during the temporary basal duration according to the temporary basal value; and  
   resuming the programmed basal rate after the temporary basal duration.

20. The method of claim 19, wherein delivering basal insulin according to the temporary basal value comprises calculating an adjusted basal rate based on the percentage of the programmed basal rate.

21. The method of claim 19, wherein delivering basal insulin according to the temporary basal value comprises replacing the programmed basal rate with the new basal rate for the temporary basal duration.

---

## Computer-Readable Medium Claim

22. A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors of an insulin pump, cause the insulin pump to perform operations comprising:  
   receiving a bolus amount, a bolus duration, and a bolus percentage entered by a user;  
   calculating an immediate bolus portion and an extended bolus portion based on the bolus amount and the bolus percentage;  
   causing delivery of the immediate bolus portion;  
   causing delivery of the extended bolus portion over the bolus duration;  
   receiving a temporary basal adjustment comprising either a percentage-based adjustment or a rate-based adjustment; and  
   causing basal delivery during a temporary basal time period according to the temporary basal adjustment.

---

counterfactuals.prompt: In formal patent language, explain a method for temporarily changing an infusion pump’s basal rate and an apparatus for delivering a medical-agent bolus using entered amount, duration, and percentage values.
counterfactuals.output:
A method for temporarily modifying a basal delivery rate of an infusion pump may be described in formal patent language as follows:

A method of operating an ambulatory infusion pump configured to deliver a medical agent to a user, the method comprising: storing, in a memory of the infusion pump, a programmed basal delivery profile defining at least one scheduled basal delivery rate; receiving, via a user interface of the infusion pump or a remote controller in communication therewith, a temporary basal-rate command including a temporary basal parameter; determining, by a controller of the infusion pump, a temporary basal delivery rate based on the temporary basal parameter and the programmed basal delivery profile; suspending, overriding, or modifying delivery according to the programmed basal delivery profile for a selected temporary basal interval; delivering the medical agent during the selected temporary basal interval at the temporary basal delivery rate; monitoring expiration of the selected temporary basal interval; and, upon expiration of the selected temporary basal interval, automatically resuming delivery according to the programmed basal delivery profile without requiring further user input.

In some embodiments, the temporary basal parameter comprises at least one of a percentage of a currently scheduled basal rate, an absolute basal rate, an increase value, a decrease value, or a duration. The controller may calculate the temporary basal delivery rate by multiplying the currently scheduled basal rate by a user-entered percentage value. The infusion pump may further limit the temporary basal delivery rate to a predetermined maximum delivery rate and may generate an alert if the entered temporary basal parameter exceeds a safety threshold.

An apparatus for delivering a medical-agent bolus using entered amount, duration, and percentage values may be described as follows:

An apparatus for delivering a bolus of a medical agent, comprising: a reservoir configured to contain the medical agent; a pumping mechanism coupled to the reservoir and configured to expel the medical agent from the reservoir to a patient; a user input device configured to receive bolus delivery parameters including an entered bolus amount, an entered delivery duration, and an entered percentage value; a memory configured to store the bolus delivery parameters; and a controller operatively coupled to the pumping mechanism, the user input device, and the memory, the controller being configured to determine, from the entered bolus amount and the entered percentage value, a first bolus portion and a second bolus portion, to cause the pumping mechanism to deliver the first bolus portion substantially immediately, and to cause the pumping mechanism to deliver the second bolus portion over the entered delivery duration.

In one embodiment, the entered percentage value represents a percentage of the entered bolus amount to be delivered as the first bolus portion, and the controller calculates the first bolus portion by multiplying the entered bolus amount by the entered percentage value. The controller may calculate the second bolus portion as a remainder of the entered bolus amount after subtracting the first bolus portion. The second bolus portion may be delivered according to a substantially uniform rate over the entered duration or according to a programmed delivery profile.

For example, if the entered bolus amount is a total bolus amount, the entered percentage value is an immediate-delivery percentage, and the entered duration is an extended-delivery duration, the controller may be configured to deliver:

1. an immediate bolus equal to the total bolus amount multiplied by the immediate-delivery percentage; and  
2. an extended bolus equal to the remaining portion of the total bolus amount, delivered over the entered duration.

The apparatus may further comprise a display configured to present the entered bolus amount, the entered duration, the entered percentage value, the calculated immediate bolus portion, and the calculated extended bolus portion for user confirmation before delivery. The controller may also be configured to compare the calculated bolus portions and delivery rates against stored safety limits, to prevent delivery if a safety limit is exceeded, and to provide an alarm or confirmation prompt to the user.
